base_model.tooltip: The model family. Picks the recommended files and the checks.

goal.tooltip: Quality = closest to bf16. Optimal = fast and near identical. Fast = fastest that still looks right.

speed_ups.tooltip: Auto = from the System & Model Optimization Report. Manual = choose each one below.

attention.tooltip: Attention backend. auto = the fastest one that passed the report's test.

fp16_accumulation.tooltip: Faster fp16 math with a small quality cost. auto = Fast goal only.

step_cache.tooltip: EasyCache: skips steps that barely change. auto = Fast goal, 20+ steps.

torch_compile.tooltip: Compiles the model: the first run is slow, later runs are faster. Needs Triton.

qwen21_cache.tooltip: Qwen-Image 2.1 only (Qwen Image 2.1 Cache): where the KV cache lives and how it is stored. auto = lossless, int8 on the Fast goal or cards under 16 GB. int8 halves the cache at about bf16 accuracy, int4 quarters it but roughly doubles the per-step error. RAM costs little speed. off = slowest.

clip_type.tooltip: Custom only: how the text encoder is loaded (CLIPLoader's type). auto = from the encoder's shape when it matches one known base model. Ignored for the other base models and for a checkpoint's own encoder.

spectrum.tooltip: MOSS Image and Krea 2: Spectrum forecasts some steps instead of running them, with no visible change in our tests (MOSS about 1.7x, Krea 2 Turbo about 1.35x, Raw about 1.6x). Built in, nothing to install. auto = Optimal and Fast goals; the first 20% of the steps always run (the layout forms there) and it sits out runs under 8 steps. off = opt out (works with speed_ups on Auto too). Replaces the step cache when on.

lora_name: Flux2\Flux2 Klein动漫转写实真人 AnythingtoRealCharacters.safetensors

image_b.tooltip: 2nd reference (subject) for multi-ref LoRAs; vision blocks in training order: scene, subject

grounding_px.tooltip: cap longest side fed to Qwen3-VL; 0 = native

system_prompt.tooltip: advanced (optional): override the grounding system prompt (empty = training default). Steers what the vision encoder attends to, e.g. facial identity detail.

Krea2EditGroundedEncode.name: Krea2EditGroundedEncode
Krea2EditGroundedEncode.description: Encodes the edit instruction grounded on the source image (training-matched semantic path).

source_latent_b.tooltip: 2nd reference (subject photo) for multi-ref LoRAs -> RoPE frame=2, training-matched order: scene first, subject second

ref_boost.tooltip: reference-fidelity dial: multiplies target->reference attention. Applies to the LAST ref (= the subject in two-ref workflows, the only ref in single-ref). 1.0 = off, >1 pulls harder toward the reference's appearance, <1 loosens. Optimal value is model-specific

ref_boost_a.tooltip: same dial for the FIRST ref (= the scene in two-ref workflows). No effect in single-ref workflows. 1.0 = off

fit_mode.tooltip: how an image source fits a mismatched output aspect ratio (needs vae + source_image connected): fit = resample the source to the target grid at a centered offset — matches how this model was trained (default, use this); crop (legacy) = center-crop to the target AR then resize (v1/v1.1 geometry, only for older weights)

ref_boost_mask.tooltip: optional region on the (last) reference to boost, e.g. the face; empty = whole reference

vae.tooltip: RECOMMENDED with source_image: enables the blur-proof pixel-space path (crop+resize in pixels, encode internally) — immune to input/output resolution mismatches

source_image.tooltip: source as IMAGE (with vae connected): overrides source_latent with exact pixel-space fitting — fixes blurry results from mismatched resolutions

target_latent.tooltip: RECOMMENDED with vae + source_image: wire the SAME latent you feed KSampler.latent_image. Lets the node VAE-encode the source here, before sampling starts, instead of on the first step — otherwise the VAE is pulled onto the GPU mid-sampling and can evict part of the diffusion model, slowing every remaining step on VRAM-tight setups

ref_position.tooltip: where the LAST reference (the person in two-image workflows, or the only image) sits in position space. aligned (trained) = pinned onto the output layout, how the models were trained (default). beside = placed next to the canvas: identity still flows but the layout pin is gone, so the person can be restaged more freely. bag of features = experimental, content without layout

ref_position_a.tooltip: the same choice for the FIRST reference (the scene in two-image workflows); no effect with a single image. For putting a person into a scene: scene aligned + person beside

Krea2EditModelPatch.name: Krea2EditModelPatch
Krea2EditModelPatch.description: Adds the krea2_edit in-context source-preservation path (source latent as frame=1 tokens) to a Krea2 model.

negative_prompt.tooltip: Existing negative prompt, if your workflow uses one.

moodboard_positive.tooltip: Positive output from a Krea Moodboard node.

moodboard_negative.tooltip: Negative output from a Krea Moodboard node.

metadata_json.tooltip: Metadata JSON from a Krea Moodboard node.

strength.tooltip: Reserved for workflow clarity; source nodes apply the style strength.

style_only.tooltip: Output only the moodboard style text, without the user prompt.

separator.tooltip: Join user prompt and style block with newlines or commas.

KreaMoodboardApply.name: KreaMoodboardApply
KreaMoodboardApply.description: Append a moodboard style block to a user prompt before Krea 2 prompt enhancement or Qwen3-VL encoding.

folder.tooltip: Root folder / subfolder under the saver output path. Tokens like %model %seed %sampler are filled in by LC Save Image from its metadata (dropped if missing).

prefix.tooltip: Used in both the path segment and the filename. Tokens like %model %seed %sampler are filled in by LC Save Image from its metadata (dropped if missing).

timestamp.tooltip: Timestamp format. Choose none to omit.

path_separator.tooltip: Path separator style. auto uses the OS default.

include_prefix_in_path.tooltip: ON: path = folder\prefix_timestamp\. OFF: path = folder\

LCAdvancedFolder.name: LCAdvancedFolder
LCAdvancedFolder.description: Split filename + path outputs for Image Saver Simple style nodes. Optional prefix-in-path and timestamp format.

LCAnySwitch.name: LCAnySwitch
LCAnySwitch.description: Pick the first connected input among many. Type-locks from the first wire. Blocks Use Everywhere auto-wiring. Dynamic 2–20 inputs.

strength.tooltip: 0 = original, 1 = full LUT, >1 overdrives the LUT change (up to 2×). Try 0.7–1.2 for most grades.

log.tooltip: OFF for normal photo/sRGB LUTs (recommended). ON only if the LUT is authored for log/linear (inverse-gamma in, gamma out).

interpolation.tooltip: tetrahedral = cleaner greys and smoother gradients, runs on the GPU (what grading apps use). trilinear = the old method.

LCApplyLUT.name: LCApplyLUT
LCApplyLUT.description: Apply a .cube 3D LUT from models/luts. Strength 0–2 (1 = full LUT, >1 overdrives). Leave log OFF for typical creative LUTs.

max_resolution.tooltip: Longer side of the output. From the image/mask: the image is scaled up or down so its longer side is this. From a preset / custom size: larger sizes shrink to it. 0 = keep the size as it is.

resolution_source.tooltip: Off: the image/mask's aspect ratio, scaled so its longer side is max_resolution (up or down). On: preset or custom width x height.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Preset ratio when using custom/preset source.

swap_dimensions.tooltip: Swap width and height after size is chosen.

upscale_method.tooltip: Resampling filter. Lanczos is a good default for photos. nvidia_rtx_vsr = RTX Video Super Resolution (RTX cards, needs nvidia-vfx): sharper, cleaner enlargements; shrinking uses lanczos.

proportion.tooltip: stretch=force size; resize=fit inside; crop=fill+crop; pad=fit+letterbox; total_pixels=match pixel budget.

crop_location.tooltip: Crop anchor when proportion is crop.

divisible_by.tooltip: Round width/height to a multiple of this (8 is typical for latents).

batch_size.tooltip: Empty latent batch. Image/mask batch is preserved from input.

LCAspectRatioPipeOut.name: LCAspectRatioPipeOut
LCAspectRatioPipeOut.description:
Resizes your image and mask to the size you want. From the image: keeps its shape and scales it up or down so the longer side is max_resolution. Or pick a preset / custom size.
Crop, stretch, pad or fit, and an empty latent at the same size.

minkowski_p.tooltip: Minkowski norm p (used by Gray Edge / Shades of Gray).

LCAutoWhiteBalance.name: LCAutoWhiteBalance
LCAutoWhiteBalance.description: Automatic white-balance correction. Pick an algorithm and blend with strength. On-node preview with before/after wipe.

intensity.tooltip: How strong the glow is. 1 = what 0.5 was before 1.53.15.

threshold.tooltip: Only what is brighter than this glows. Lower = more of the picture glows.

smoothing.tooltip: How gently the glow fades in around the threshold. 0 = a hard cut.

radius.tooltip: How far the glow spreads. Scales with the picture size.

saturation.tooltip: Colour of the glow. 0 = white, 1 = the light's own colour.

exposure.tooltip: Brightness of the glow, on top of intensity.

mode.tooltip: Bloom = glow from bright areas. Pro-Mist = a diffusion filter in front of the lens (soft glow, gentler contrast, blacks kept deep). Halation = the red-orange glow film gets around bright edges.

look.tooltip: Pick the same look on LC Depth FX, Bloom, Lens Profile, Vignette, Film Stock and Film Grain and they match. Custom = your own sliders. Moving a slider switches to Custom.

LCBloom.name: LCBloom
LCBloom.description: Bloom / glow from bright areas. Threshold, radius, intensity. On-node preview + wipe.

state.tooltip:
True → on_true, False → on_false.
💡 Rename the on_true or on_false socket (right-click it > Rename Slot) and this switch shows those names, e.g. Upscale / Skip. Not renamed: it shows the title of the node wired in.

on_true.tooltip: Passed through when state is true. Rename this socket to rename the switch's true state.

on_false.tooltip: Passed through when state is false. Rename this socket to rename the switch's false state.

LCBooleanSwitch.name: LCBooleanSwitch
LCBooleanSwitch.description: Boolean switch: state picks on_true or on_false (any type). Only the picked branch runs. Rename the on_true / on_false sockets and the switch's two states take those names.

list_file.tooltip: List file under assets/lists/ (one term per line, # comments ok).

enabled.tooltip: DISCLAIMER: a convenience filter, not a safety system. It only removes the exact words in the list, it cannot understand an image or a prompt, and it will miss things. It does not make any content allowed. You alone are responsible for what you create and post, and for following CivitAI's Terms of Service and the law. No guarantee the list is complete, current or enough for approval. Not affiliated with CivitAI. Off = the text passes through untouched. You have to switch it on yourself.

LCCivitaiStrip.name: LCCivitaiStrip
LCCivitaiStrip.description: CivitAI 🚩🔪: removes listed words and phrases (whole words only) from a prompt, for example the "child" / "late teens" wording LLMs (abliterated models especially) sometimes add to adults. Off until you switch it on. DISCLAIMER: a convenience filter, not a safety system. It only removes the exact words in the list, it cannot understand an image or a prompt, and it will miss things. It does not make any content allowed. You alone are responsible for what you create and post, and for following CivitAI's Terms of Service and the law. No guarantee the list is complete, current or enough for approval. Not affiliated with CivitAI.

preset.tooltip: Starting preset. Moving any slider switches this to Custom.

sharpen.tooltip: Capture sharpening. Undoes the softness measured in the picture (deconvolution) instead of drawing outlines, so an upscaled 4K image is not over-sharpened. 0 = off.

strength.tooltip: Mix with the original. 0 = original, 1 = full effect.

halo.tooltip: Halo control. 1 = edges can not overshoot their neighbours (no bright/dark rims). 0 = allow punchy overshoot.

skin_protect.tooltip: Less sharpening, texture and clarity on skin, and pores can not be dug into pits. Eyes, lashes and lips still get sharpened. 0 = off (use 0 for anime and lineart).

radius.tooltip: Detail size. Low = fine lines and hair. High = softer images and broader structure. Scales with resolution.

blend_mode.tooltip: How clarity is blended. Soft Light is the most natural, Overlay and Hard Light punch harder.

shadow_protect.tooltip: Less effect in dark areas (keeps shadow noise down). 0 = full effect.

highlight_protect.tooltip: Less effect in bright areas. 0 = full effect.

texture.tooltip: Mid-size detail: pores, fabric, fur, pencil hatching. 0 = off.

skin_mask.tooltip: Optional. The skin skin_protect covers (white = skin), e.g. LC Skin Master's skin_mask. Unwired, skin is found by colour, which misses some skin.

LCClarity.name: LCClarity
LCClarity.description: Sharpen Pro: capture sharpening (deconvolution), texture and clarity on luminance only. Halo control stops rims, flat areas stay clean. Presets fill the sliders.

method.tooltip: oklab = matches the whole colour cloud (how the colours relate, not each channel on its own) in a colour space built for the eye; out-of-range colours roll off instead of clipping. oklab + distribution = also matches the cloud's shape (separate colour groups, different tints in shadows and highlights); slower. adain = old per-channel mean/std match; mean_std = the same in linear light.

reference.tooltip: Color reference (style). If empty, node bypasses and passes image through. oklab methods: a reference batch the same size as the image batch matches frame to frame; any other batch is pooled into one look (adain / mean_std use only the first reference).

skin_protect.tooltip: Hold original skin hue and cap skin chroma gain after match (0=off, 1=full). Lightness still follows the match.

mask.tooltip: White = apply match. Black = keep image. Leave empty for full frame (old graphs unchanged).

LCColorMatch.name: LCColorMatch
LCColorMatch.description: Match colors to a reference (Oklab full-colour match, or the old AdaIN / mean-std). Optional skin_protect holds face hue. Optional mask: white = match, black = keep image. No reference = bypass. On-node preview + wipe.

LCComboSelector.name: LCComboSelector
LCComboSelector.description: Dropdown that mirrors another node’s combo options (scheduler, sampler, etc.) when wired into a converted combo input.

LCControlPanel.name: LCControlPanel
LCControlPanel.description: One panel of sliders and switches, each with its own output. The gear at the end of a row sets its type (number or boolean), name, min, max, step and decimals (0 = INT, otherwise FLOAT). Plug a new row into a number or boolean input and it copies that input's name, range and value. Double-click a number to type one.

model.tooltip:
Depth Anything V2 weights. The license is in the label: Small is Apache-2.0, Base / Large / Giant are CC-BY-NC-4.0 (non-commercial).
Uses the file you already have (models/depthanything or comfyui_controlnet_aux), or downloads it the first time you run.

resolution.tooltip: Size the shorter side is processed at (rounded to a multiple of 14). 518 is what the model was trained at; higher can add detail on big images.

invert.tooltip: Off: bright = near (what Depth Anything and depth ControlNets use). On: bright = far.

LCDepthAnythingV2.name: LCDepthAnythingV2
LCDepthAnythingV2.description: Depth Anything V2 depth map, normalized 0-1 per image. Bright = near unless invert is on. Outputs a 3-channel image and a MASK of the same map.

depth_map.tooltip: Depth map of the same image (LC Depth Anything). Either direction works.

look.tooltip: Pick the same look on LC Depth FX, Bloom, Lens Profile, Vignette, Film Stock and Film Grain and they match. Custom = your own sliders. Moving a slider switches to Custom.

haze.tooltip: How thick the air is. Distant areas fade toward the haze color. 0 = off. 0.06 - 0.16 for people, more only for wide landscapes.

haze_distance.tooltip: Where the haze starts, measured across the background: 0 = right behind the subject, higher = only its farthest part.

haze_warmth.tooltip: The haze color comes from the image's own distance. This nudges it cooler (-) or warmer (+).

light_wrap.tooltip: Bright background light bleeding over the subject's edges. Kills the cut-out sticker look. 0 = off.

dof_blur.tooltip: Depth of field. How blurry things get away from the focus. 0 = off. Scales with resolution.

focus_range.tooltip: How much depth stays sharp around the focus. Low = razor thin (like f/1.4), high = deep (like f/8).

bokeh.tooltip: Bright out-of-focus lights turn into glowing discs. 0 = plain blur.

auto_focus.tooltip: Focus on the main subject in the middle of the frame. Off = use focus_depth.

focus_depth.tooltip: Used when auto_focus is off. 0 = nearest, 1 = farthest.

depth_direction.tooltip: Leave on Auto unless the effects land on the wrong part of the image.

focus_mask.tooltip: Optional. Focus lands on whatever this mask covers (a face or person mask from LC MaskMaker). Beats auto_focus when connected.

LCDepthFX.name: LCDepthFX
LCDepthFX.description: Depth-driven camera effects: atmospheric haze, light wrap and depth of field with real bokeh. Wire a depth map from LC Depth Anything. Pick a look or set the sliders. On-node preview with before/after wipe.

sampler.tooltip: From KSamplerSelect, LC Sigmas or ClownSampler (any SAMPLER).

amount.tooltip:
How much detail. The same scale as the original Detail Daemon: 0.25 = the model is told 2.5% less noise at the peak. Negative = smoother. Not multiplied by CFG.
Put it on the low pass sampler. Detail is made in the last steps; on the high pass it moves the layout.
Krea 2 / Krealism: look only 0.5 to 1.0, start 0.15, end 0.85, peak 0, exponent 0. classic and keep structure hit harder: start lower. At 16+ steps use less. Samplers that add their own noise (dpmpp_2m_sde, euler_ancestral, er_sde, res_* / ClownSampler with eta): lower it, or it can leave specks.

start.tooltip: The step where it begins: 0 = first step, 1 = last. Early steps shape folds and fabric.

end.tooltip: The step where it ends. Leave the last steps alone, or noise can stay in the image.

peak.tooltip: Where in the window it is strongest (the original's bias): 0 = right at start, on the noisy steps, where it shapes things (works best); higher = later, a gentler sharpen.

exponent.tooltip: The ramp's curve: 0 = flat, full strength across the whole window (works best); 1 = a smooth bump; above 1 = narrower.

mode.tooltip: look only = the model sees less noise, but its answer is rescaled to the real noise: crisp, without big reshuffles. classic = the original Detail Daemon (more detail, small things shift). keep structure = classic, but only the fine part of the change is kept, so the layout stays (two model calls per step in the window).

sigmas.tooltip: Draws the graph only. Wire the sigmas of the sampler this feeds (sigmas_low for the low pass). The window always follows that sampler's own steps.

LCDetailDaemon.name: LCDetailDaemon
LCDetailDaemon.description:
Adds fine detail by telling the model there is a little less noise than there really is, in a window of the steps. Same scale and window as the original Detail Daemon, plus keep structure mode, and no CFG maths.
Put it on the low pass sampler. Detail is made in the last steps.

pipe.tooltip: LC_PIPE from Pipe In/Edit, Aspect, Sampler, or KJ Get.

LCDetailPipeOut.name: LCDetailPipeOut
LCDetailPipeOut.description: Unpacks what a detailer needs from a pipe: model, clip, VAE, prompts, seed, CFG, sampler, scheduler and detailer steps. The pipe keeps going out the top. protect_mask (bottom): the areas the pipe detailers redrew.

angle.tooltip: Blur direction in degrees, screen convention: 0 = right, 90 = down.

distance.tooltip: Blur length in pixels. 0 = no blur.

strength.tooltip: Blend toward the blurred result. The blur itself is a hard, full-strength smear over its length -- turn this down rather than the distance if it's too much.

taps.tooltip: How many samples are averaged along the path (WAS Node Suite's `taps`). Low (2-8) reads as a visibly stepped multi-exposure ghost instead of a smooth streak -- an effect in its own right, not just a quality knob. High (64+) is smooth even on a long distance.

edge.tooltip: What the blur reads past the image border. 'hold the edge' repeats the border pixel outward. 'mirror' folds the image back on itself (this node's original, only behavior). 'empty' reads black past the edge, which darkens the border as the smear runs off it.

LCDirectionalBlur.name: LCDirectionalBlur
LCDirectionalBlur.description: Motion-style directional blur -- every pixel smears along one angle/length vector. Drag the arrow on the node's face to set it (angle from the arrow's direction, length from how far you drag), or type exact values. 0 length or 0 strength is a no-op. `taps` and `edge` match WAS Node Suite's Image Directional Blur -- fewer taps gives a stepped multi-exposure look instead of a smooth streak, and `edge` picks what the blur reads past the image border. On-node preview + wipe.

LCDynamicOverlay.name: LCDynamicOverlay
LCDynamicOverlay.description: Overlay image B on A. A sets resolution; B is fit-scaled. After one run, adjust opacity on the node without regenerating.

grain_size.tooltip: Grain radius at 1024px reference; scales with resolution.

look.tooltip: Pick the same look on LC Depth FX, Bloom, Lens Profile, Vignette, Film Stock and Film Grain and they match. Custom = your own sliders. Moving a slider switches to Custom.

response.tooltip: Where the grain shows. classic: mostly the midtones (the old behavior). film: strongest in the shadows and midtones, fading out in the highlights, like a negative. sensor: phone / digital camera noise, it grows with the light (shot noise) but reads strongest in the shadows, and blue is the noisiest channel.

LCFilmGrain.name: LCFilmGrain
LCFilmGrain.description: Film grain overlay with amount, contrast, scale, and mono vs color grain. response: classic (midtones), film (shadows and midtones) or sensor (phone / digital camera noise). On-node preview with before/after wipe. For a video, use LC Film Grain (Video).

look.tooltip: Pick the same look on LC Depth FX, Bloom, Lens Profile, Vignette, Film Stock and Film Grain and they match. Custom = your own sliders. Moving a slider switches to Custom.

LCFilmStockBW.name: LCFilmStockBW
LCFilmStockBW.description: Black-and-white film stock look from presets. Strength blends the effect. On-node preview + wipe.

look.tooltip: Pick the same look on LC Depth FX, Bloom, Lens Profile, Vignette, Film Stock and Film Grain and they match. Custom = your own sliders. Moving a slider switches to Custom.

LCFilmStockColor.name: LCFilmStockColor
LCFilmStockColor.description: Color film stock look from presets (toe/shoulder/gamma). Strength blends. On-node preview + wipe.

LCGetImage.name: LCGetImage
LCGetImage.description: Reads resolution and batch size from an image. Outputs megapixels, width, height, resolution (longer side in pixels), batch, and aspect ratio (e.g. 1.0:1.2).

x.tooltip: Crop left edge as % of image width (0–100).

y.tooltip: Crop top edge as % of image height (0–100).

width.tooltip: Crop width as % of image width (0.5–100).

height.tooltip: Crop height as % of image height (0.5–100).

aspect.tooltip: Lock crop aspect ratio. 'original' matches the source image.

LCImageCrop.name: LCImageCrop
LCImageCrop.description: Windows-style interactive crop: drag the box and handles on the node. Optional aspect lock (free / original / common ratios). x,y,width,height are percentages of the source.

radius_multiplier.tooltip: Kernel radius scale relative to blur strength

mode.tooltip: smart = measures the noise in each image and cleans brightness and colour noise separately, keeping pores and hair (uses luma / chroma / keep_detail). legacy = the old edge-gated blur (uses blur_strength / edge_preservation / radius_multiplier).

luma.tooltip: smart: how hard brightness noise (grain) is cleaned, relative to the noise measured in the image. 1 = tuned default, 0 = leave brightness alone.

chroma.tooltip: smart: how hard colour noise (blotches, rainbow speckle) is cleaned. Colour edges follow the brightness edges, so they stay sharp. 0 = leave colour alone.

keep_detail.tooltip: smart: how much of the original texture comes back where it stands clearly above the noise (pores, hair, fabric). Smooth areas stay clean either way.

LCImageDenoise.name: LCImageDenoise
LCImageDenoise.description: Denoise. smart: measures the noise in each image, cleans brightness and colour noise separately and keeps pores and hair. legacy: the old edge-gated blur. On-node preview with before/after wipe.
output_tooltips: The denoised image.
smart mode: the noise measured in each image (brightness and colour, out of 255).

match_aspect_ratio.tooltip: On: keep the incoming image/mask ratio. The larger of the current width/height settings is the long side. Off: use preset or custom W×H as-is.

aspect_ratio.tooltip: Preset size, or custom to use custom_width × custom_height.

custom_width.tooltip: Target width for custom size. Also the size source (with height) when match_aspect_ratio is on.

custom_height.tooltip: Target height for custom size. Also the size source (with width) when match_aspect_ratio is on.

upscale_by.tooltip: none = use the size above. multiplier = scale that size. megapixels = set total pixels at the current ratio.

multiplier.tooltip: Scale factor when upscale_by is multiplier. Steps of 0.25, max 4.00.

megapixels.tooltip: Target megapixels when upscale_by is megapixels. Steps of 0.01, max 8.00.

upscale_method.tooltip: Resampling filter. Lanczos is a good default for photos. Masks use nearest. nvidia_rtx_vsr = RTX Video Super Resolution (RTX cards): sharper enlargements; shrinking uses lanczos.

proportion.tooltip: stretch=force size; resize=fit inside; crop=fill+crop; total_pixels=match pixel budget (custom W×H).

crop_location.tooltip: Crop anchor when proportion is crop.

divisible_by.tooltip: Final width/height are floored to a multiple of this, then the image/mask is resampled to that size. 16 for Z-Image / Flux; 8 for SDXL. 1 = off.

LCImageMaskResize.name: LCImageMaskResize
LCImageMaskResize.description: Resize an image and/or mask to a preset or custom W×H. match_aspect_ratio uses the larger settings side and keeps the input ratio. upscale_by can then multiply that size or set megapixels. Final size is a multiple of divisible_by.

image.tooltip: Picture to turn, crop and pad.

keep_frame.tooltip:
keep: the turn and frame stay as you set them, run after run. Use it when you rerun the same picture (post processing, same seed).
snap back after run: once a run finishes, the turn and frame go back to the plain picture, so the next image starts clean.

angle.tooltip: Turn in degrees, clockwise. Or drag the round handle on the node (hold Shift for 15° steps).

fit.tooltip:
expand: the frame starts around the whole turned picture, and the empty corners are masked for the model to paint.
crop: the frame starts at the largest box with no empty corners.

fill.tooltip: What goes in the new area before the model paints it. gray is what Krea 2 and AnyPaint expect. edge stretches the outer pixels out (for models that copy what they see).

left.tooltip: Frame left edge, % of source width. Positive pads, negative crops.

top.tooltip: Frame top edge, % of source height. Positive pads, negative crops.

right.tooltip: Frame right edge, % of source width. Positive pads, negative crops.

bottom.tooltip: Frame bottom edge, % of source height. Positive pads, negative crops.

aspect.tooltip: Lock the output shape. 'original' matches the source picture.

snap_to.tooltip: Round the output width and height up to a multiple of this (extra goes right and bottom). 1 = off.

block.tooltip:
until turned or framed: while the picture is untouched (no turn, no crop, no pad), or a new picture comes in, the run stops after this node. Set it up on the picture shown here, then Run: with LC123 it carries on with the same seeds, so only what comes after runs.
never: always passes the picture on, even untouched.

max_megapixels.tooltip: Stops the edges from being dragged past this canvas size, so the canvas never grows bigger than the model handles well (Krea 2 and AnyPaint like about 2). Only limits dragging: the run itself is never resized. 0 = no limit.

LCImageRotatePad.name: LCImageRotatePad
LCImageRotatePad.description: Turn, crop and pad a picture by dragging on the node: the round handle turns it, the frame edges pad (drag out) or crop (drag in). The mask covers the new area and the corners a turn opens up.
output_tooltips: The turned, cropped and padded picture.
White where the model paints: the padding and the corners a turn opens up.
Output width.
Output height.

upscale_method.tooltip: Resampling method. nvidia_rtx_vsr = RTX Video Super Resolution (RTX cards, needs nvidia-vfx): sharper enlargements; shrinking uses lanczos.

megapixels.tooltip: Target size in megapixels (1.0 = 1,000,000 pixels, the same count LC Get Image uses). The aspect ratio is kept.

resolution_steps.tooltip: Width and height are rounded to a multiple of this (8, 16, 32, 64 for models that need it). 1 = off.

LCImageToTotalMegapixels.name: LCImageToTotalMegapixels
LCImageToTotalMegapixels.description: Scale an image to a total megapixel count, like Scale Image to Total Pixels. Also outputs the resulting resolution (longer side in pixels) and megapixels.

value.tooltip: BOOLEAN, INT, FLOAT, or number. Non-zero / True → true, else false; then inverted.

LCInvertBoolean.name: LCInvertBoolean
LCInvertBoolean.description: Same multi-type coercion as LC Boolean, then invert the result. Shows true/false on the face.

model.tooltip: Krea 2 (Turbo). The LoRA and patches are added for this node only.

clip.tooltip: Krea 2 text encoder (Qwen3-VL 4B, CLIP type krea2).

mask.tooltip: White = paint, black = keep. Optional: no mask with LC Outpaint's canvas uses its mask. Wire LC Outpaint's control_image as the image and control_mask as the mask to outpaint.

prompt.tooltip: Describe the WHOLE finished picture, not just the change: "a woman in a red coat on a snowy street". Removal-only prompts ("remove the car") tend to leave a flat blob.

lora: Flux2\Flux2 Klein动漫转写实真人 AnythingtoRealCharacters.safetensors

lora.tooltip: yijunwang2's krea2_anypaint_rank32 (models/loras). Applied at lora_strength for this node only.

lora_strength.tooltip: 1.0 is what it was trained for.

steps.tooltip: 8 (Krea 2 Turbo). The keep is exact with euler.

sampler_name.tooltip: euler is what AnyPaint was trained and tested with; the keep step is exact only for euler.

crop_to_mask.tooltip: On: a small mask is redrawn in its own crop, scaled up to inpaint_resolution (more detail). Off: the whole picture at inpaint_resolution.

padding.tooltip: Context around the mask when cropping (px). More = the model sees more of the scene.

inpaint_resolution.tooltip: Size of the redraw (as an area: 1024 = about 1 MP). AusBoss found above about 1.6 MP Krea 2 starts to crease limbs and darken skies.

boundary_px.tooltip: Border around the mask the model redraws to blend the seam (in redraw pixels). 32 = the reference.

vlm_reference.tooltip: Show the reference to the text encoder too. On = the reference recipe.

composite.tooltip: keep original = only the painted area (soft edge, colour fixed) is pasted back: everything else is exactly your picture. raw = the model's whole redraw of the crop.

LCKrea2AnyPaint.name: LCKrea2AnyPaint
LCKrea2AnyPaint.description:
Inpaint and outpaint for Krea 2 with yijunwang2's AnyPaint LoRA, done the way it was trained: a whole-canvas reference, the kept pixels put back after every step, and a border the model blends. Your picture outside the mask comes back unchanged. Describe the whole finished picture in the prompt.
Outpaint: wire LC Outpaint's control_image and control_mask in.
output_tooltips: Your picture with the masked area painted.
Where it was pasted back (soft edge).

mode.tooltip: Add character or try to correct it.

strength.tooltip: How much lens character. 1 = what 0.5 was before 1.53.15.

look.tooltip: Pick the same look on LC Depth FX, Bloom, Lens Profile, Vignette, Film Stock and Film Grain and they match. Custom = your own sliders. Moving a slider switches to Custom.

LCLensProfile.name: LCLensProfile
LCLensProfile.description: Apply or correct a named lens profile (aberrations character). Strength scales the effect. On-node preview with before/after wipe.

LCLiftGammaGain.name: LCLiftGammaGain
LCLiftGammaGain.description: Lift / gamma / gain style grade (shadows, midtones, highlights) plus offset. On-node preview with before/after wipe.

normal_map.tooltip: Normal map of the same image (LC Normal Map).

depth_map.tooltip: Depth map of the same image (LC Depth Anything V2).

preset.tooltip: A starting look. Picking one sets the lights and shadows below, then you can adjust anything. Editing a light or shadow value switches this to custom.

blend.tooltip: How much of the relit result is mixed over the original. 0 = original, 1 = fully relit. 0.7 to 0.9 looks best.

light1_type.tooltip: spot = a soft beam that lights part of the frame. sun = even light over the whole frame.

light1_x.tooltip: Where the light is on the stage: X = left/right, Y = down/up, Z = how frontal (0 side-on, 1 head-on). Drag the handle on the stage, or type here.

light1_y.tooltip: Where the light is on the stage: X = left/right, Y = down/up, Z = how frontal (0 side-on, 1 head-on). Drag the handle on the stage, or type here.

light1_z.tooltip: Where the light is on the stage: X = left/right, Y = down/up, Z = how frontal (0 side-on, 1 head-on). Drag the handle on the stage, or type here. Z changes the shading and the beam. It does not change the shadow length.

light1_brightness.tooltip: How bright the light is. About 1.2 to 1.5 is a natural key light.

light1_spread.tooltip: Spot only: how wide the beam is. Small = tight spotlight, large = soft flood over the whole face.

light1_warmth.tooltip: Color of the light. Negative = cool blue, 0 = neutral, positive = warm orange.

light1_color.tooltip: Optional colored gel on this light. Works together with warmth. The color only shows where this light reaches, so shadows fall back to the neutral fill.

light1_color_amount.tooltip: How strong the colored gel is. 0.3 to 0.6 looks natural, 1 is a saturated stage light.

enable_light_2.tooltip: Add a second light (fill or rim).

light2_type.tooltip: spot = a soft beam that lights part of the frame. sun = even light over the whole frame.

light2_x.tooltip: Where the light is on the stage: X = left/right, Y = down/up, Z = how frontal (0 side-on, 1 head-on). Drag the handle on the stage, or type here.

light2_y.tooltip: Where the light is on the stage: X = left/right, Y = down/up, Z = how frontal (0 side-on, 1 head-on). Drag the handle on the stage, or type here.

light2_z.tooltip: Where the light is on the stage: X = left/right, Y = down/up, Z = how frontal (0 side-on, 1 head-on). Drag the handle on the stage, or type here. Z changes the shading and the beam. It does not change the shadow length.

light2_brightness.tooltip: How bright the light is. About 1.2 to 1.5 is a natural key light.

light2_spread.tooltip: Spot only: how wide the beam is. Small = tight spotlight, large = soft flood over the whole face.

light2_warmth.tooltip: Color of the light. Negative = cool blue, 0 = neutral, positive = warm orange.

light2_color.tooltip: Optional colored gel on this light. Works together with warmth. The color only shows where this light reaches, so shadows fall back to the neutral fill.

light2_color_amount.tooltip: How strong the colored gel is. 0.3 to 0.6 looks natural, 1 is a saturated stage light.

light_wrap.tooltip: Softens where light turns to shade on the face and body. 0 = a sharp line like a hard lamp, higher = a gradual roll-off.

fill.tooltip: Base light that everything keeps, including the shadow side. 0 = pitch black shadows, 0.2 = natural, 0.5 = flat.

shadows.tooltip: soft = edges soften away from the object. hard = sharp edges (sun, spotlight). off = no cast shadows, only shading.

shadow_amount.tooltip: How dark cast shadows get. They never go below the fill light.

shadow_blur.tooltip: Blurs the edges of cast shadows, in both soft and hard mode. Raise it if a shadow looks cut out.

background_shadow.tooltip: How much of the shadow shows on the background behind the subject. 1 = a wall right behind, 0 = a distant background with nothing near enough to catch a shadow. Uses the mask if connected, otherwise the depth map.

self_shadow.tooltip: Needs a mask. How strongly the subject shadows itself (nose, chin, hair) compared with the shadow it throws on the background.

relief.tooltip: How deep the face and scene are in 3D. More = longer, stronger shadows from noses, chins and hair.

advanced.tooltip: Show the fine controls (depth, shadow shape, mask options).

depth_falloff.tooltip: Far areas get less light. 0 = no falloff.

shadow_height.tooltip: Height of the light for SHADOWS only. Low = long stretched shadows, high = short shadows right under things. Separate from Light Z.

shadow_length.tooltip: The farthest a shadow can reach (fraction of the image).

shadow_softness.tooltip: Soft shadows only: how quickly the edge softens with distance from the object.

subject_distance.tooltip: Needs a mask. How far the subject stands in front of the background, so it throws a shadow on it. 0 = flat against the wall.

mask_dome.tooltip: Needs a mask. Blends a rounded shape over the subject to smooth the form shading.

mask.tooltip: Subject mask (LC Remove Background / LC Person Mask). Optional.

LCLightingControlV2.name: LCLightingControlV2
LCLightingControlV2.description: Relight an image from a normal map and a depth map with one or two lights (spot or sun), warmth, and real hard or soft cast shadows. Pick a preset, drag the light on the stage, and blend it back over the original.

model.tooltip: Diffusion model to apply the enabled LoRAs to. Optional: leave unconnected for a clip-only chain.

clip.tooltip: CLIP to apply the enabled LoRAs to. Optional: leave unconnected for a model-only chain.

lora_rows.tooltip: Internal: the row list (on/lora/strength), maintained by the node's own face. Not meant to be typed by hand.

LCLoraLoader.name: LCLoraLoader
LCLoraLoader.description: Apply any number of LoRAs to a model/clip from one node: enable, name and strength per row, drag to reorder, an Info button that reads the LoRA's own trigger words. model and clip are both optional, so you can use this for a model-only or clip-only chain. Rows disabled or at 0 strength are skipped.

strength.tooltip: How much of the AI look is taken out. 0.4 - 0.75 for most renders (1 = what 0.5 was before 1.53.15).

skin.tooltip: How much orange / plastic skin is calmed, and how much flat skin is left out of the fine-texture lift, on top of strength. 0 = skin untouched and sharpened like the rest (use 0 after LC Skin Master).

LCNaturalLook.name: LCNaturalLook
LCNaturalLook.description: Takes the AI look out: loud colours and orange skin calmed, highlights rolled off, glossy glow reduced and fine texture lifted, with the original black point, contrast and brightness kept. Before/after wipe on the node.

image.tooltip: Image to estimate surface normals for.

model: scannet.pt (BAE normals, ScanNet-trained; license unclear, verify before commercial use)

model.tooltip:
BAE weights (scannet.pt). Trained on ScanNet, whose terms are not commercial-friendly, and the weights' Hugging Face card just says 'other'. Verify before commercial use.
Uses the copy you already have (models/normalbae or comfyui_controlnet_aux), or downloads it the first time you run.

resolution.tooltip: Size the shorter side is processed at. 512 is what ControlNet uses; higher is slower and can add detail.

flip_y.tooltip: Flip the green channel (OpenGL vs DirectX style normal maps).

blur_radius.tooltip: Blur the finished normal map with ComfyUI's Blur Image. The radius is in pixels, the blur kernel is 2 x radius + 1 wide. Smooths the fine noise BAE leaves on flat surfaces. 0 = no blur.

sigma.tooltip: How evenly the blur spreads across its radius (same meaning as in Blur Image). Higher = stronger, closer to a plain box blur. Lower = gentler, weighted toward the center. Only used when blur_radius is above 0.

LCNormalBAE.name: LCNormalBAE
LCNormalBAE.description: BAE surface normal map (RGB = XYZ), the same style ControlNet's normal_bae makes. Optional blur (blur_radius, sigma) uses ComfyUI's Blur Image.

image.tooltip: Image with a person in it.

engine.tooltip:
segformer: higher resolution. Body = arms and legs only (bare torso and neck read as clothes).
mediapipe: body includes torso and neck skin. Needs the mediapipe package.

segformer_model.tooltip: Used by the segformer engine. Entries marked 'Download' are fetched the first time you run.

body.tooltip: Skin below the face. See engine for what counts.

accessories.tooltip: Hats, glasses, shoes, bags (and whatever else the model calls an accessory).

confidence.tooltip: How sure the model must be. Lower grows the selection, higher shrinks it.

refine.tooltip: Edge refinement of the raw mask. vitmatte is best for hair, guided_filter is fast, none keeps the raw mask.

vitmatte_model.tooltip: Only used when refine is vitmatte.

edge_erode.tooltip: Trimap: how far the sure-foreground is pulled in from the mask edge (pixels).

edge_dilate.tooltip: Trimap: how far the unknown band reaches out past the mask edge (pixels).

black_point.tooltip: Mask values at or below this become 0.

white_point.tooltip: Mask values at or above this become 1.

max_megapixels.tooltip: vitmatte only. Larger images are matted at this size, then scaled back.

remove_features.tooltip: Cut the eyes, eyebrows, lips and teeth out of the face, using SAM 3 (the model LC Segment Anything and LC Smart Detailer use). With engine mediapipe and face + body on, this is a skin-only mask for LC Skin Beauty, LC Skin Upscale or LC Sharpen Pro. Only runs when face is on.

LCPersonMask.name: LCPersonMask
LCPersonMask.description: Select parts of a person: face, hair, body, clothes, accessories, background. Segformer or MediaPipe, with optional guided filter / VITMatte refine. Skin only: mediapipe, face + body, remove_features on (cuts eyes, brows, lips and teeth with SAM 3).

preset.tooltip: Same 37 looks as WAS Node Suite's Image Style Filter -- 1977, Aden, Brooklyn, Xpro2, and the rest.

strength.tooltip: Blend toward the graded result. 1 = full look, 0 = original image.

LCPhoneFilters.name: LCPhoneFilters
LCPhoneFilters.description: 37 phone-app style presets (same set as WAS Node Suite's Image Style Filter). Pick a look, dial strength, drag the on-node wipe to compare.

LCPipeEdit.name: LCPipeEdit
LCPipeEdit.description: Packs anything you wire into one pipe, so one wire carries it all. Wire a pipe in to change only what you connect; everything else rides along.

pipe.tooltip: LC_PIPE from Pipe In, Pipe Edit, or KJ Get.

LCPipeOut.name: LCPipeOut
LCPipeOut.description: Unpacks a pipe back into separate sockets. The pipe keeps going out the top. protect_mask (bottom): the areas the pipe detailers redrew, for LC Skin Upscale / LC Skin Texture protect_mask.

image.tooltip: Image to show. Nothing connected or a null signal is fine: the node just waits.

LCPreviewImage.name: LCPreviewImage
LCPreviewImage.description: Preview an image. If no signal arrives it sits there quietly without an error.

mask.tooltip: Mask to show (white = masked). Nothing connected or a null signal is fine: the node just waits.

LCPreviewMask.name: LCPreviewMask
LCPreviewMask.description: Preview a mask. If no signal arrives it sits there quietly, black, without an error.

clip.tooltip: CLIP model from a checkpoint / CLIP loader.

string.tooltip: Prompt text — wire from a Positive/Negative or other STRING node.

LCPromptToConditioning.name: LCPromptToConditioning
LCPromptToConditioning.description: Encode a text prompt into CLIP conditioning. String is socket-only.

image.tooltip: A picture, a batch of pictures, or the frames of one video (see source).

source.tooltip: video: the frames are matched to each other, so they stay steady. image: each picture is upscaled on its own, so nothing carries over between them.

upscale.tooltip: 2x for video, 4x for pictures. Each is its own 5.2 GB model, downloaded on first use.

seed.tooltip: One step from noise: the seed only changes the finest grain.

detail.tooltip: How much of the added detail is kept. 1.0 = full model output, lower moves toward a plain bicubic upscale.

LCRelayVSRUpscale.name: LCRelayVSRUpscale
LCRelayVSRUpscale.description: RelayVSR upscale in one node (ComfyUI 0.44 or newer). Fast and sharp, adds fine skin and hair detail. 2x for video, 4x for pictures. Models download on first use (Comfy-Org/RelayVSR, Apache-2.0). Keeps VRAM flat on 8 GB cards.
output_tooltips: The upscaled frames. Held in RAM at full size: a 5 s clip at 4x is about 12 GB.
For LC Save Video's relay input: it decodes and saves the video a few frames at a time, so it never sits in RAM. With only this output connected, the full-size image is never built.

image.tooltip: Image to cut the subject out of.

model.tooltip:
Background removal model. The license is in the label.
Entries marked 'Download' are fetched the first time you run.

refine.tooltip:
none: use the model's mask as is.
guided_filter: fast, snaps the edge to the image.
vitmatte: matting model for hair and fine detail.

vitmatte_model.tooltip: Only used when refine is vitmatte.

grow.tooltip: Pixels to grow (positive) or shrink (negative) the mask before refining.

edge_erode.tooltip: Refine trimap: how far the sure-foreground area is pulled in from the mask edge. Smaller = tighter.

edge_dilate.tooltip: Refine trimap: how far the unknown band reaches past the mask edge. Smaller = tighter.

black_point.tooltip: Mask values at or below this become 0. Raise it to clear faint background haze.

white_point.tooltip: Mask values at or above this become 1. Lower it to solidify the subject.

max_megapixels.tooltip: vitmatte only. Larger images are matted at this size, then scaled back.

background.tooltip: Color behind the subject in the on_background output.

LCRemBG.name: LCRemBG
LCRemBG.description: Remove the background with BiRefNet. Outputs an RGBA cutout, the mask, and the subject on a solid color. Optional guided filter or VITMatte refine.

total_steps.tooltip: Total sampling steps for the full schedule.

step_swap.tooltip: Step index where the first pass hands off to the second (SplitSigmas step).

detailer_steps.tooltip: Steps reserved for a detailer / refiner stage (0 = unused).

denoise.tooltip: Denoise strength used when building the sigma schedule (1.0 = full).

LCSamplerConfigure.name: LCSamplerConfigure
LCSamplerConfigure.description: All your two-pass sampler settings in one place: steps, swap step, detailer steps, denoise, both CFGs, sampler and scheduler.

images.tooltip: Batch to save. Each frame is a file.

filename.tooltip: File stem. Easy Folder can still be wired if you prefer one combined prefix. %model %seed %steps %cfg %sampler %scheduler %denoise %width %height are filled in from the metadata socket; missing ones are dropped.

path.tooltip: Subfolder under Comfy output. Empty = output root. Separators normalized. Name tokens like %model work here too.

format.tooltip: PNG keeps workflow + CivitAI text chunks. JPEG/WebP only get a short comment.

quality.tooltip: JPEG / WebP quality. Ignored for PNG.

embed_workflow.tooltip: Write Comfy prompt + workflow JSON into the PNG.

embed_civitai.tooltip: Write A1111-style parameters from the metadata socket.

hash_resources.tooltip: SHA-256 AutoV2 of checkpoints, UNET, CLIP, VAE, LoRAs found in the graph. CivitAI lists resources from these hashes, not from names.

metadata.tooltip: From LC Save Metadata. Prompts, seed, models, CivitAI AIR/URL.

filename_prefix.tooltip: Optional combined prefix (Easy Folder). Used when filename is left as default and this is wired.

LCSaveImage.name: LCSaveImage
LCSaveImage.description: Save images with Comfy workflow metadata. Wire LC Save Metadata for CivitAI parameters. filename + path widgets; PNG recommended.

pipe.tooltip: LC_PIPE in. Fills prompts, seed, steps, CFG, sampler, scheduler, size, denoise. Widgets override.

seed_value.tooltip: Seed. -1 = use pipe seed if present. Plain INT — no control-after-generate.

models.tooltip: Checkpoint names. Model 1 and Model 2 in one field, comma-separated.

civitai_air.tooltip: CivitAI AIR or model URL. Several are fine, comma-separated (e.g. the model and your workflow page). No hash lookup. Fill it to link your workflow/model on CivitAI. Trade-off: CivitAI then labels the image "made on-site". Leave it empty and the image reads as an external generator (models and LoRAs still match by hash).

width.tooltip: 0 = the width of the image LC Save Image actually saves (upscaled or not). Any other number is written instead.

height.tooltip: 0 = the height of the image LC Save Image actually saves (upscaled or not). Any other number is written instead.

extra_params.tooltip: Appended to the parameters line (LoRAs, hashes, notes).

LCSaveImageMetadata.name: LCSaveImageMetadata
LCSaveImageMetadata.description: Save metadata for LC Save Image. Optional LC_PIPE in (no pipe out). Models are one comma-separated string. civitai_air takes one or more AIRs or URLs, comma-separated.

base_seed.tooltip: A number = that exact fixed seed, reused every run. -1 = a fresh random number every run. Use the node's own buttons rather than typing -1 by hand: 'Randomize Each Time' sets this to -1, 'New Fixed Random' rolls one number now and writes it here as a real fixed seed. Capped below 2**64 on purpose -- see the module docstring.

LCSeed.name: LCSeed
LCSeed.description: Utility seed. Type a fixed number, or use the node's face: 'Randomize Each Time', 'New Fixed Random', manual entry, or pick one of the last 10 seeds this node actually ran with.

LCShowText.name: LCShowText
LCShowText.description: Show a string on the node (ShowText-style). Keeps newlines; JSON pretty-prints. Pass-through STRING out.

model.tooltip: The first pass's model. Its noise range and sigma shift set the schedule.

sampler.tooltip: The sampler both passes use (the sampler output). With RES4LYF installed its samplers are listed too, and a ClownSampler Selector can be wired in. The line under the graph shows what tested best for your model.

sigma_curve_presets.tooltip:
The curve the steps follow, from noisy to clean.
base = a plain scheduler (base_scheduler).
beta = the beta curve with your own alpha and beta.
flowmatch = the FlowMatch Euler Discrete curve.
hyperbolic = the base curve bent by sinh / cosh / tanh.
gaussian = the base curve bent by a bell curve.
saved: = a curve you saved. Drag the points on the graph to bend any of them.

base_scheduler.tooltip: The scheduler under base, hyperbolic and gaussian (sigma_curve_presets). Flow models (Krea 2, Z-Image, Flux 2): beta, beta57 and simple are safe; karras, kl_optimal and linear_quadratic burn.

step_swap.tooltip: The step where the second model (model_2) takes over. 0 = one pass only.

denoise.tooltip: How much of your input image gets redrawn. 1 = a new image from scratch (text to image).

denoise_steps.tooltip: full schedule = denoise covers the whole run; the second pass just carries on. at step swap = denoise covers the first pass only; the second pass refines on its own.

low_pass.tooltip: What the second pass does at the step swap. continue noise schedule = it takes the leftover noise and finishes the job (one schedule over two samplers). renoise = the first pass finishes the picture, then fresh noise goes back up to the swap point's level, so the second pass has something to refine, like a detailer.

scheduler_shape_2.tooltip: The second pass's curve. same as first = the schedule above, curve edits included.

first_pass_resample.tooltip: Walks the first pass in more (or fewer) steps along the same path; where it starts and stops stays put. 1 = off. 1.15 = 15% more first-pass steps.

sigma_shift.tooltip: Bends the schedule without changing the step count. Higher = more steps on composition (the noisy start), lower = more on detail. use model default = what the model was trained with. by image size = Flux's rule (needs image_size_latent). custom = custom_shift. SDXL-type models have no shift. flowmatch and saved curves ignore it.

custom_shift.tooltip: The model's own shift number. Krea 2 / Flux: 0.5 small images, 1.15 = Krea 2 Turbo's default, 2+ = strongly composition-heavy.

beta_alpha.tooltip: beta: higher = more steps at the noisy start.

beta_beta.tooltip: beta: higher = more steps at the clean end (detail).

flowmatch_shift.tooltip: flowmatch: the curve's shift (used when flowmatch_dynamic is off).

flowmatch_dynamic.tooltip: flowmatch: dynamic shifting (as in V23.2) or the fixed flowmatch_shift.

flowmatch_terminal.tooltip: flowmatch: stretch the curve so the last step lands here. 0 = off.

hyperbolic_function.tooltip: hyperbolic: the function that bends the base curve.

hyperbolic_scale.tooltip: hyperbolic: how hard the function bends it.

gaussian_mean.tooltip: gaussian: where the bell curve sits (a noise level).

gaussian_std.tooltip: gaussian: how wide the bell curve is.

gaussian_operation.tooltip: gaussian: how the bell curve bends the base curve.

edit_mode.tooltip: Dragging a point on the graph: smooth pulls its neighbours along, spike moves only that point.

smooth_radius.tooltip: smooth: how many steps around the point come along.

curve_edit.tooltip: Your curve edit (set by dragging on the graph).

model_2.tooltip: The second pass's model, if different (e.g. without ControlNet). Its own schedule, lined up.

image_size_latent.tooltip: Only for sigma_shift = by image size: the empty latent, so the shift can follow the image size.

LCSigmas.name: LCSigmas
LCSigmas.description: One scheduler for one- and two-pass sampling: schedule presets (base, beta, flowmatch, hyperbolic, gaussian, your saved curves) you can bend by dragging on the graph, the step swap to a second model, image-to-image denoise, what the second pass does (continue or renoise), and the noise and sampler for each pass.
output_tooltips: First pass (or the only pass).
Second pass, from the step swap.
Noise for the first sampler.
Noise for the second sampler (none when it continues the schedule).
What the schedule does, in words.
The whole first-model schedule, unsplit.
The chosen sampler, for SamplerCustomAdvanced.

preset.tooltip: Natural: grit out, blemishes evened, a touch cooler, pores and character kept. Clean Even Tone, Soft Beauty, Editorial Detail (close-ups), Real Skin Restore (plastic skin), Mature Skin (age kept), Weathered (lines deepened), Body Skin, Sun-Kissed (freckles). Moving a slider switches to Custom.

clean.tooltip: Grit out: pixel speckle and colour noise on the skin. Pores and freckles stay.

pores.tooltip: The skin's own fine texture: 1 = as it is, higher = crisper, lower = softer. Keep at 1 or more with pigmentation.

add_pores.tooltip: Real pore relief from a skin photo, on skin that has none (plastic AI skin). Skin that already has detail gets less.

pore_size.tooltip: Size of the added pores and freckles. 1 = sized to the face.

even_skin.tooltip: Spots, blotches and uneven patches evened. The pores and the face's shape are kept.

wrinkles.tooltip: Below 0 softens creases and lines. Above 0 deepens the lines already there into real creases.

even_colour.tooltip: Redness and colour patches pulled towards the skin's own colour.

pigmentation.tooltip: Freckles where the sun lands (nose, cheekbones, forehead), grown from the ones already there and in their colour.

eye_detail.tooltip: Brows and lashes: crisper and deeper. Needs a face.

warmth.tooltip: Below 0 cooler (calms orange AI skin), above 0 warmer.

brightness.tooltip: Lighter or darker skin. Highlights are eased off.

saturation.tooltip: More or less colour in the skin.

shadow_lift.tooltip: Opens up dark skin in shadow.

seed.tooltip: Changes the added pores and freckles.

mask.tooltip: Skin to work on (white). For body skin wire LC Person Mask (face + body). Unwired: faces are found for you, body skin only partly (facexlib, about 80 MB downloaded into models/facexlib on the first run).

delicate_skin.tooltip: Lips and other delicate skin are found and treated lightly, their colour kept.

skin_match.tooltip: Higher finds more skin (and more skin-coloured cloth).

LCSkinMaster.name: LCSkinMaster
LCSkinMaster.description: The whole skin chain in one node: grit out, pores, blemishes, lines, freckles, eyes, skin tone and colour, each done once on one face-aware skin map. Presets from a light clean-up to plastic-skin restore, weathered and sun-kissed. Outputs the skin_mask for other nodes. On-node before/after wipe.

LCSlider.name: LCSlider
LCSlider.description: On-node slider face. Min / max / step / decimals in Settings. Outputs INT or FLOAT. Works with Nodes 2.0.

pipe.tooltip: LC pipe: model, VAE, seed, steps, cfg, sampler and scheduler come from here.

prompt.tooltip:
What to detail, as simple words separated by commas: hands, face.
Every match is found (both hands, every face). Add :N to cap it, e.g. face:1.

sam3_model.tooltip: SAM 3 model that does the finding. Pick the SAM 3.1 download, or use your own sam3.pt / sam3.safetensors in models/sam3.

threshold.tooltip:
How sure SAM 3 has to be. Lower finds more (and more wrong things), higher is pickier. 0.5 is a good start.
Colors are only a hint: 'red dress' can still pick a green dress. Things that are not there are not found.

grow.tooltip: Pixels to grow (positive) or shrink (negative) the mask before inpainting. Growing a little covers the edges.

feather.tooltip: Softness of the mask edge in pixels, so the redrawn area blends into the rest. 0 = hard edge.

blend.tooltip: How much of the redraw is pasted in: 1 = all of it. Below 1 the old and new pixels are mixed, and features the redraw moved a little (lashes, eyelids) can show twice. For a lighter redraw, lower denoise instead.

padding.tooltip: Pixels of the surrounding image included with each crop, so the model sees the context.

inpaint_resolution.tooltip: Each crop is redrawn at about this many pixels squared (1024 = 1 megapixel), whatever its shape. Higher = more detail, slower.

denoise.tooltip: How much is redrawn. Low keeps the shape and fixes details, high redraws from scratch.

image.tooltip: Optional. Empty = the pipe's image. Wire one when a node without a pipe changed the picture in between.

model.tooltip: Optional. Wire a model here to use it instead of the pipe's (with LoRAs on it, or a different model).

vae.tooltip: Optional. Wire a VAE here to use it instead of the pipe's.

positive.tooltip: The image's prompt. A prompt describing the whole scene can get drawn into every crop at denoise 0.3 and up (a whole tiny scene in the face): wire inpaint_positive to prevent that.

inpaint_positive.tooltip: Optional. A prompt for the crops only, e.g. 'close-up of a woman's face, natural skin'. Used instead of positive for the redraw. Recommended whenever positive describes the whole scene.

negative.tooltip: Optional. Leave empty for cfg 1 models; wire it for SDXL and other models that use a negative.

tone_match.tooltip: On: the redraw gets the original's brightness, contrast and colour back where it is pasted, keeping the new detail. A light redraw comes back a little flat and dull without it. Turn off when the redraw is meant to change colours (a new shirt colour, a different object).

cfg.tooltip: CFG for the redraw. 1 works for Krea 2, Flux, Z-Image and, at detailer denoise (up to about 0.4), SDXL too (tested: SDXL looked the same at cfg 1 to 7). Used instead of the pipe's cfg_1, which is usually the main sampler's.

LCSmartInpaintPipe.name: LCSmartInpaintPipe
LCSmartInpaintPipe.description:
Finds what you describe (hands, face, eyes, etc.) and redraws it at full detail. Each hand or face gets its own crop, scaled up to inpaint_resolution, redrawn, then blended back in. Nothing found? The image passes through untouched and the node tells you.
No negative wired: fine for Flux, Krea 2, Anima and other cfg 1 models. Wire one for SDXL.

sampler.tooltip: High pass sampler only. From LC Sigmas, KSamplerSelect or LC Detail Daemon.

auto.tooltip: Picks the grow step from the run's own schedule (about 2x faster, same quality).

grow_at_step.tooltip: Used when auto is off. The step where the picture grows to full size, counted like step_swap. 0 = every step at full size.

LCSpeedBoost.name: LCSpeedBoost
LCSpeedBoost.description:
BETA. Plug it into the high pass sampler only. It starts the picture at half size and grows it to full size partway through: about 2x faster, same quality. The layout follows the model's trained size, so a seed frames differently with it on.
Put LC Detail Daemon on the low pass. Detail is made in the last steps.
Speeds up passes that start from noise (denoise 0.9 and up). Upscale and image to image passes run as normal: their layout comes from your image.
Works on Krea 2, Z-Image, Flux.2 Klein, Qwen-Image, Wan, and SDXL / Pony / Illustrious (about 1.4x there). On Flux 3 Klein auto grows early (about 1.2x) so text and small faces stay clean. On MOSS Image it grows at noise 0.85 (about 1.6x, 2.4x with the 8-step LoRA). It switches itself off on inpaint masks and MOSS layout boxes (the console says why). On Qwen-Image 2.1 auto stays off: line art, text and flat color break at its half size. Set grow_at_step by hand for photos.
Based on SPEED (Xiao, Chao, Yariv and Wetzstein, 2026).

enable.tooltip: ON: stop here (mxStop behaviour). OFF: pass through without stopping.

LCStop.name: LCStop
LCStop.description: Queue breakpoint with an enable switch. When enabled, stops until you continue from the queue/play control. Bypass/off passes data through without stopping.

text.tooltip: Text to draw (wraps at edges with a small margin)

font.tooltip: Font family (curated list — changes apply on queue; live preview uses matching CSS name)

x_percent.tooltip: X position (% from left). Drag on preview or use the widget.

y_percent.tooltip: Y of the top of the text block (% from top). Default near bottom. Drag or use the widget.

alignment.tooltip: Horizontal alignment: left / center / right. Legacy *-top/center/bottom values still load and map to left/center/right.

LCTextOverlay.name: LCTextOverlay
LCTextOverlay.description: Draw text on an image. Drag on the preview to place; font size/color/position update live. Multiline with edge margin.

image.tooltip: Picture to mask. A Load Image upstream shows up right away, anything else after one run.

sam3_model.tooltip: Finds the edges. The same SAM 3 model LC Segment Anything and LC Smart Detailer use.

person_parts.tooltip: On a person, taps grow by body part (face, hair, head, clothes, person) with the Segformer model LC Person Mask uses. off: SAM 3 decides every step.

block.tooltip: if_empty_mask: when nothing is selected, or a new picture comes in from a run, everything downstream stops so you can select on the picture shown, then Run (with LC123 it carries on with the same seeds). A new picture in a Load Image shows here right away, so it doesn't stop.

grow.tooltip: Grow (or shrink, below 0) the finished mask by this many pixels.

invert.tooltip: Flip the mask (everything but the selection).

selections.tooltip: Internal: what you drew and tapped.

threshold.tooltip: How sure a pixel must be to join. Lower takes in more (wispy hair, soft edges), higher is tighter.

smooth.tooltip: Cleans the edge: fills pinholes, drops stray specks and rounds jagged edges, without shrinking the selection. 0 = raw.

refine.tooltip: Edge finish on the run (the preview shows the selection before it). guided_filter: fast, follows the picture's edges. vitmatte: best for hair, slower. none: the hard selection.

LCTouchMask.name: LCTouchMask
LCTouchMask.description: Mask one thing exactly: draw around it and SAM 3 finds its edges. Tap it to grow to the next bigger thing (face, + hair, head, person), double-tap to step back. Ctrl + draw cuts out.

pipe.tooltip: LC pipe: the picture comes from its image.

upscale_by.tooltip: Final size. 1.25x to 4x are one pass: smaller is lighter (1.5x is about a third faster than 2x). 6x and 8x run two passes (3x + 2x, 4x + 2x): one big pass breaks the skin up into patches.

seed.tooltip: VOSR2 is one step from noise: the seed only changes the finest grain.

color_alignment.tooltip: Keeps the result's colours on the input's. wavelet = best match.

tile_size.tooltip: Pixel tiles for the upscale model. VOSR2 was trained at 512: keep it there.

vae_tile_size.tooltip: Pixel tiles for its VAE. Lower = less VRAM, a little slower.

image.tooltip: Optional. Empty = the pipe's image. Wire one when a node without a pipe changed the picture in between.

LCVOSRUpscalePipe.name: LCVOSRUpscalePipe
LCVOSRUpscalePipe.description: LC VOSR2 Upscale on the LC pipe: upscales the pipe's picture (what the detailers left in it) and puts the result back in the pipe, with the detailers' areas resized to it ('protected' output).
output_tooltips: The pipe with the upscaled picture, and the detailers' areas resized to it.
The upscaled picture.
The faces and hands the detailers redrew, at the new size. Wire it into LC Skin Texture / LC Skin Upscale protect_mask so they do not add skin detail on top of the detailers' work.

any.tooltip: Any input — passed through unchanged after cache clear.

LCVRAMCacheClear.name: LCVRAMCacheClear
LCVRAMCacheClear.description: Pass-through *any* node that clears GPU/model cache when it runs. Place between heavy stages, or on its own branch off a heavy stage.

LCVibrance.name: LCVibrance
LCVibrance.description: Smart saturation (vibrance) and optional plain saturation; skin-tone protection. On-node preview with before/after wipe.

intensity.tooltip: Darken edges. Negative = brighten edges. 0.1 - 0.25 = a real lens. 1 - 2 with cos4 off = an old photo, up to black corners.

midpoint.tooltip: Where the darkening starts. Lower = closer to the middle.

feather.tooltip: How soft the edge is. Low = a hard oval, high = a long gentle fade.

cos4_falloff.tooltip: On: real lens light falloff. Off: a printed / old-photo vignette with a smooth edge that can go all the way to black.

look.tooltip: Pick the same look on LC Depth FX, Bloom, Lens Profile, Vignette, Film Stock and Film Grain and they match. Custom = your own sliders. Moving a slider switches to Custom.

LCVignette.name: LCVignette
LCVignette.description: Edge darkening or brightening vignette. On-node preview with before/after wipe.

size_percent.tooltip: Watermark width as % of base width. Live on node after first run.

opacity.tooltip: Opacity 0–1. Live on node after first run.

x_percent.tooltip: Horizontal center %. Drag on preview to set.

y_percent.tooltip: Vertical center %. Drag on preview to set.

margin_percent.tooltip: Edge padding as % of image (small, similar to Text Overlay ~6px).

watermark_mask.tooltip: The watermark's transparency. Load Image splits a transparent PNG into IMAGE + MASK: wire its MASK here and the see-through parts of your logo stay see-through.

LCWatermark.name: LCWatermark
LCWatermark.description: Composite a watermark image. Drag to place; size and opacity update live after the first run. No watermark input = bypass.

clip.tooltip: The text encoder (Krea 2, MOSS Image, Anima, SDXL, Illustrious, Pony ...).

text.tooltip: The prompt. Its words show below, ready to weight.

strength.tooltip: How strongly every weight acts. Lower it if a weighted word starts to break the picture up.

weights.tooltip: The word weights (set on the node).

model.tooltip: Krea 2 and MOSS Image need the model: their weights work inside the model. Other models don't.

edit_conditioning.tooltip: Not needed: the weights find their words in any Krea 2 encoding (wire this node's prompt into the edit encoder instead). Wired, this conditioning comes out as the node's own.

block.tooltip: With the prompt socket wired. on change: the box takes the incoming prompt when it changes, your edit holds until then. always: the box holds, and a new incoming prompt stops the run here: edit, then Run carries on with the same seeds. never: the incoming prompt always comes through (✎ switches to on change, so an edit holds).

last_in.tooltip: The incoming prompt of the last run (set on the node).

prompt.tooltip: Optional: a prompt from another node. It lands in the box, where you can edit and weight it (see block).

LCWeightedPrompt.name: LCWeightedPrompt
LCWeightedPrompt.description: A text encoder with a weight per word: click a word, move its slider. Green = more, red = less, below 0 = taken out. Works on Krea 2 and MOSS Image (inside the model) and on Anima and CLIP models (SDXL, Illustrious, Pony).
output_tooltips: The model, with the word weights built in on Krea 2 and MOSS Image (wire it to the sampler).
The encoded prompt.
The prompt used (your edit, or the linked one), without weights: wire it into an edit encoder or metadata.
The prompt with (word:weight) written in, for metadata or another encoder.

model.tooltip: The diffusion model the LoRA will be applied to.

clip.tooltip: The CLIP model the LoRA will be applied to.

lora_name: Flux2\Flux2 Klein动漫转写实真人 AnythingtoRealCharacters.safetensors

strength_model.tooltip: How strongly to modify the diffusion model. This value can be negative.

strength_clip.tooltip: How strongly to modify the CLIP model. This value can be negative.

LoraLoader.name: LoraLoader
LoraLoader.description: This LoRA loader is used to modify both diffusion and CLIP models, altering the way in which latents are denoised such as applying styles. Multiple LoRA nodes can be linked together.
output_tooltips: The modified diffusion model.
The modified CLIP model.

lora_name: Flux2\Flux2 Klein动漫转写实真人 AnythingtoRealCharacters.safetensors

LoraLoaderModelOnly.name: LoraLoaderModelOnly
LoraLoaderModelOnly.description: This LoRAs loader is used to modify the diffusion model, altering the way in which latents are denoised such as applying styles. Multiple LoRA nodes can be linked together.
output_tooltips: The modified diffusion model.
The modified CLIP model.

PreviewImage.name: PreviewImage
PreviewImage.description: Preview the images without saving them to the ComfyUI output directory.

vae.tooltip: The VAE model used for decoding the latent.

VAEDecode.name: VAEDecode
VAEDecode.description: Decodes latent images back into pixel space images.
output_tooltips: The decoded image.
